elaine-support: FYI customer reported a failing tool/function call when sending binary from the TypeScript SDK. They pass a Buffer/Uint8Array as the tool arg and get a schema validation error from the API: 

Error: 400 Bad Request - invalid_tool_args
{ "message": "tool arg 'image' expected string, got object" }

Repro steps (from customer):
1) Node 18, ts-sdk@1.6.2
2) snippet:
```ts
const img = fs.readFileSync('scan.png');
await client.callTool('ocr', { image: img });
```
3) server returns above 400 and tool is not invoked.

They say the same payload via curl (base64 string) succeeds. Suspect SDK is serializing Buffer -> { type: 'Buffer', data: [...] } which fails our tool schema (expects base64 string). Can someone confirm? @tim-sdk can you triage? :eyes:

jordan-eng: Can you paste the raw outbound payload from the customer's network capture? If SDK is sending the Node Buffer object as-is we need a patch. Also need customer id and example request_id to look up server logs.

elaine-support: Customer request_id: req_2026-03-15_ACME_337. Raw body (trimmed):
```
{"tool":"ocr","args":{"image":{"type":"Buffer","data":[137,80,78,71,13,10,26,10,...]}}}
```
They attached full PCAP but wanted quick triage.

tim-sdk: Confirmed repro on ts-sdk@1.6.2. We're currently JSON.stringify-ing args without special-casing Buffer/Uint8Array. Node Buffer becomes the object you pasted. Python SDK encodes bytes -> base64 by default, which is why curl works.

Workaround for customers: send base64 yourself: `client.callTool('ocr', { image: img.toString('base64') })` or prefix with `data:image/png;base64,${...}` if tool expects mime. I'll push a hotfix to detect Buffer/Uint8Array and auto-base64 encode.

maria-ml: Is there any risk that auto-encoding will change tool selection (router) behavior? Some tools infer type by seeing `image:` as object vs string. If we change to base64 string, router should still pick image tools but double-check. Could also add Content-Type hint in the arg: `{image:{__data__: 'base64...', mime: 'image/png'}}` — but that changes schema.

tim-sdk: Good call. Proposed fix: (a) transparently encode Buffer/TypedArray to base64 string, (b) include a short wrapper when sending to the control plane: `{__redwood_bytes__: 'base64...', mime: optional}` so router + servers can distinguish. Also update server-side schema to accept either a base64 string or wrapper. I'll open a PR with unit tests.

elaine-support: Customer asks for ETA — can you give an ETA for hotfix? They are on a paid Dedicated plan.

Tim-sdk: Hotfix branch created: `fix/ts-buffer-encode-189876`. Patch included and unit tests added. Will run CI now. If green I'll merge + release a patch 1.6.3 today. If we need a faster route, we can ship a npm patch just for the serialization module.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging -> canary -> production (expected start 1898765900).

jordan-eng: Once patch is live we should backfill an integration test that simulates router/tool selection when image arg is sent as Buffer vs base64 so we don't regress. Also add monitoring to catch similar schema mismatch errors (invalid_tool_args) grouped by sdk-client header.

tim-sdk: Will add test + monitoring. I'll post PR link and changelog when merged. For now please send the workaround to the customer (base64) and escalate billing SLA if they need hotter support.

elaine-support: Thanks — sending workaround and ETA. Will follow up when customer verifies. :thumbsup:
